concerns.text: Tasks T005-T009 (Phase 1) and T010-T014 (Phase 2) are exact duplicates (e.g., T005/T010 both create scaffolding, T006/T011 both implement utils.py). This violates the deterministic execution model by creating redundant, conflicting work items for the same deliverables, effectively weakening the plan's structural integrity.

Task T017 instructs to 'log a warning and proceed with synthetic data only' if external fetch fails. While FR-001 designates synthetic as primary, the task's logic implies an attempt to fetch external data as a standard step. This risks violating Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) if the system attempts to fetch unverified external sources before falling back, or creates a silent failure mode not explicitly authorized by the spec's 'MAY' clause for external data.

Task T038 describes shuffling interaction terms to calculate a p-value but omits the mandatory comparison of error distributions between an Additive Model and an Interaction Model. FR-005 explicitly requires a 'Permutation Test comparing the error distributions of an Additive Model and an Interaction Model'. T038's description suggests a single-model permutation importance test, which is a semantic weakening of the required statistical methodology.

Task T039 conflates 'Permutation Importance' (>0.01) with the 'Permutation Test p-value' (<0.05). SC-003 requires BOTH metrics to validate the hypothesis. T039 only addresses the importance threshold, dropping the explicit verification of the p-value threshold in this specific task step, which fragments the acceptance criteria for SC-003.

Task T020 specifies imputing missing values with 'mean of series'. The spec's Edge Cases explicitly require imputation using the 'mean of the specific alloy series'. 'Mean of series' is ambiguous (could mean global mean of the column) and fails to preserve the stricter constraint of imputing within the specific alloy group, potentially introducing bias not permitted by the spec.
